sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster, at a 20.5% CAGR to $155.2 billion, lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F31][F40][F223][F41][F50].
FY2026 was the sharpest step, with revenue up 17.8% to $331.8 billion driven by Microsoft Cloud, Azure and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [F10][D472][P17].
FY2018 net income fell 35.0% to $16.6 billion on the TCJA charge, and FY2019 rebounded 136.8% to $39.2 billion with a $2.6 billion intangible-transfer tax benefit [F52][D48][F53][D101][P61].
Microsoft Cloud reached 64.6% of revenue in FY2026 and contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% growth [D566][D568][D472].
Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp, with Azure and other cloud services growing 41% on demand across workloads [D642][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 revenue per user [D649][P14].
More Personal Computing shrank 1.1% as XBOX revenue fell 7%, partly offset by Search advertising up 9% [D941][P10][P9].
Incremental operating margin was 53.3% in FY2026, with revenue growth 10.3pp above operating-cost growth [D498][D499].
Operating margin of 46.8% is a window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as cost of revenue grew 21.1% against 17.8% revenue growth [F30][D486][D981][D489][D472].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
Operating expenses rose 7.4%, driven by R&D compute capacity, AI talent, XBOX impairment and Copilot advertising [D491][P16].
Net margin jumped 4.2pp to 40.3% partly on $6.5 billion of OpenAI investment gains in other income [F70][D488][P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $182.9 billion, 55.1% of revenue, but free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion as capex reached $115.9 billion [F100][D477][D457][F120][D478][F110].
Free cash flow was 0.50x net income, a window low against a 0.91x median, and 20.2% of revenue versus a 30.3% median [D460][D988][D990][D456][D984].
Capex ran at 3.38x D&A and 34.9% of revenue, with investing outflow up $66.9 billion mainly on a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions [D461][D455][P1].
Operating cash flow growth came from higher cash received from customers and lower income-tax payments, partly offset by supplier payments [P1].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell to $40.3 billion while cash and investments held at $113.2 billion, and the current ratio of 1.23x is a window low [D464][D463][F200][D991].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted count fell 0.2% [X147][X157][D468][D493].
Return on average equity of 34.0% sits at the peer median of 38.8% despite the highest operating margin in the group [D471][D1011][D998].
Free cash flow stayed below 80% of net income for two years, at 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026, the lowest conversion in the window [R1][D406][D460][D988].
Operating cash flow still covered net income 1.37x, while capex consumed 34.9% of revenue [D459][D455].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated upward, so FY2017 ratios and the FY2018 tax-rate comparison rest on first-reported values [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
The FY2017 recasts are low-severity and do not change the trend, but the multi-year free-cash-flow squeeze is the number that matters [R2][R1].
Free cash flow margin: a recovery above the 30.3% window median would reverse the capex-led squeeze, while a print below the 20.2% FY2026 low would confirm it, in the FY2027 10-K [D984][D982].

Operating margin: holding above the 46.8% FY2026 high would extend the leverage trend, while a drop below the 41.7% median would signal AI infrastructure costs biting, in the FY2027 10-K [D974][D975].
Capex against revenue: a move back under the 22.9% FY2025 level would ease the cash drag, while staying at or above 34.9% keeps free cash flow depressed, in the FY2027 10-K [D401][D455].
